body:
What Owners and Leasing Professionals Need to Know About the Future of Office Occupancy

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping the modern workplace faster than any technological wave since the Internet. Across every industry, AI is automating tasks, streamlining operations, and redefining how work gets done.

Yet amid all the forecasts of massive job losses, the commercial office market must focus on what truly matters: How will these changes affect office-using employment — the white-collar sectors that occupy most leased space in major U.S. cities.

Today, approximately 163 million Americans are employed, with roughly one-third working in traditional office-using sectors such as law, accounting, finance, insurance, real estate, consulting, and technology.

Over the next decade, studies from McKinsey, Brookings, and the World Economic Forum suggest that 8–15% of total U.S. employment could be structurally affected by AI automation.

However, this does not mean those jobs vanish entirely. Instead, many roles will evolve — requiring human oversight, creativity, and relationship-building — skills that AI cannot replace.

For owners and leasing professionals, this means the market will not collapse; it will reconfigure. Expect 15–25% reductions in average space demand per tenant as hybrid work and automation take hold. Consider too, that new growth from AI, cybersecurity, data analytics, life sciences, and professional training sectors will occur.

The office is not disappearing. It is being redefined.

The Context: What’s Really Changing

The last three years have already triggered a profound reset in office use. The pandemic normalized hybrid work, driving companies to reduce footprints by 20–30%. Now, AI is accelerating the next phase of transformation.

According to McKinsey’s 2024 report “Generative AI and the Future of Work in America,” up to 30% of U.S. work hours could be automated by 2030. But this change will unfold unevenly—task by task, firm by firm—rather than through sudden mass layoffs.

The MIT confirms that data-heavy white-collar jobs—legal research, accounting, compliance, analysis—face the greatest disruption, while judgment-based, creative, and relationship-driven roles remain essential.

Companies will not eliminate entire divisions; they will reshape them.
The result: fewer repetitive roles, more analytical and client-facing staff, and more flexible collaboration space in offices.

Who Occupies Offices Today

These industries form the backbone of Class A and B office occupancy nationwide—and are the same sectors undergoing AI-driven realignment. Each is evolving toward leaner operations but more specialized space.

AI Exposure by Sector: Who’s at Risk

Most reductions will occur in lower and middle layers (clerical, entry-level, and analyst roles) while senior professionals remain indispensable for client trust, ethics, and leadership.

Why Firms Still Need Junior People

AI may automate early tasks, but it cannot train future leaders.

A law firm that outsources all document review has no associates to become partners.
An accounting firm without junior auditors has no pipeline for future CPAs.

Every industry still requires a learning ladder — young professionals gaining institutional knowledge, mentorship, and culture through in-person collaboration.

That’s why major employers are reinforcing office expectations:

  • Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley: in-office mandates for junior bankers to learn by osmosis.
  • Deloitte, EY: hybrid but training-intensive, using AI alongside rotational mentoring.
  • Kirkland & Ellis, Latham & Watkins: large urban offices maintained for real-time learning.

Mentorship and collaboration will keep offices full, even in the AI age.

Why In-Office Work Is a Competitive Advantage

AI boosts productivity, but in-person collaboration builds innovation and culture.
Leading firms now view their offices not as overhead, but as strategic assets for:

  • Faster onboarding and peer learning
  • Stronger team cohesion
  • Confidentiality and cybersecurity
  • Creativity and innovation
  • Client trust and relationship-building

Examples:

  • Salesforce: teams in the office 3+ days closed 18% more deals than remote ones.
  • Amazon: requires in-office presence for collaboration and invention.
  • Bank of America: mandates three days for analysts, five for executives to maintain mentorship continuity.

AI may enable remote work but people still perform best together.

Projected Space Scenarios (2025–2035)

Even under aggressive forecasts, office use does not disappear. It evolves into smaller, smarter, more flexible space, focused on collaboration and training.

Who Will Fill Offices Going Forward

While traditional sectors may shrink modestly, others are expanding quickly.
The Southeast and Atlanta in particular are emerging as AI and innovation hubs.

Growth Sectors in Office Demand

(Note: sectors like government, public programs, and sustainability will expand more slowly given current political and budget headwinds.)

Key Players Expanding in Atlanta & the Southeast

  • Fortinet – 215,000 sf innovation campus in Atlanta
  • AIG – 600-job digital AI hub, Brookhaven
  • Google – 500,000 sf Midtown campus
  • Visa – 123,000 sf Midtown innovation office
  • BlackRock – Expanding fintech teams in Atlanta
  • Equifax – Collaborative data offices in Alpharetta
  • Delta Air Lines – Tech Square “Hangar” innovation center
  • Home Depot – AI and analytics labs at HQ
  • UPS – Sandy Springs logistics AI expansion
  • Oracle – Nashville riverfront headquarters campus
  • ReliaQuest – Tampa HQ with cybersecurity labs
  • Citadel Securities – 1.3M sf Miami HQ tower
  • Wells Fargo / Bank of America / Truist – Charlotte AI and innovation hubs
  • Kaseya – Miami-based IT growth hub
  • Red Hat / IBM / SAS – Expanding analytics divisions in RTP

These companies are driving the next cycle of leasing activity in the region—combining high-tech operations with training-intensive hybrid workforces.

What This Means for Owners and Leasing Professionals

Short-Term (1–3 Years)

  • Expect high sublease inventory and flight-to-quality.
  • Focus marketing on tech-enabled Class A buildings.
  • Offer plug-and-play and short-term (2–4 year) leases for agility.

Mid-Term (3–7 Years)

  • Retrofit older assets for collaboration, sustainability, and amenity-rich experiences.
  • Convert excess space into labs, training, or co-working suites.
  • Target co-location deals: AI + finance, health + tech, logistics + data.

Long-Term (7–10 Years)

  • Demand stabilizes with smaller footprints but higher rent per square foot.
  • Offices evolve into brand experience centers—where teams innovate, meet clients, and develop future leaders.
  • Landlords who align early with these new occupiers will capture the next wave of growth.

Strategic Opportunities

  • Target growth sectors: AI, cybersecurity, fintech, data analytics, health-tech.
  • Use AI in leasing: predictive analytics for renewals, tenant prospects, and pricing.
  • Partner with universities: Georgia Tech, Emory, Duke, Clemson, and UNC for workforce programs.
  • Design smarter space: collaboration zones, tech infrastructure, flexible meeting areas.
  • Market community: emphasize that offices create culture, learning, and mentorship.

Final Thoughts: The Future Is Smarter, Not Smaller

AI is not eliminating office work — it’s redefining it.

While total headcount may decline modestly, the importance of physical space as a center for culture, collaboration, and learning will rise.

Commercial real estate is not facing extinction. It is entering a new era of purpose.
The office of the future will be a hub of human innovation, where technology, mentorship, and creativity converge.

Landlords, investors, and leasing professionals who adapt now by targeting the right sectors and redesigning for flexibility will thrive in the years ahead.

The next chapter isn’t about empty buildings.
It’s about smarter buildings, filled with people doing higher-value work.

title: CRM and AI are Transforming CRE: Do You Have a Personal Impact Program (PIP)?
excerpt: As the CRM and AI revolution accelerates, my firm—focused on branding and marketing—along with my co-author, Brett Hunsaker (a.k.a. Mr. Shoomze) take a closer…
body:
As the CRM and AI revolution accelerates, my firm—focused on branding and marketing—along with my co-author, Brett Hunsaker (a.k.a. Mr. Shoomze) take a closer look at how these powerful tools can effectively grow your business while still prioritizing the art of building personal relationships.

Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platforms, enhanced with Artificial Intelligence (AI), are transforming commercial real estate (CRE). By automating routine tasks, tracking interactions, predicting client behaviors, and offering tailored insights, CRMs help CRE professionals operate more effectively and efficiently than ever before.

Leading CRM platforms such as Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, HubSpot, and specialized solutions like Yardi and AscendixRE have become invaluable tools in today's competitive CRE landscape. AI-powered platforms like DeepSeek, ChatGPT, and xAI further empower professionals by predicting client needs, automating client communication, and facilitating data-driven decision-making.

Many large CRE firms have developed proprietary CRM and AI programs, but the true focus should remain on fostering and strengthening personal relationships.

Yet, amidst all these technological advancements, one core truth remains unchanged: commercial real estate is fundamentally built upon personal relationships. 

The Essential Balance: CRM and the Personal Impact Program (PIP)

CRMs equipped with AI capabilities provide powerful benefits. For instance, they can automatically send birthday wishes, remind teams about client anniversaries, and flag meaningful milestones. But these automated processes alone, while efficient, can feel sterile and transactional.

Here is where a deliberate human-centered strategy makes all the difference—a clearly defined approach we call the Personal Impact Program (PIP). This program emphasizes that authentic, meaningful interactions must be intentionally integrated alongside technology-driven communication.

Why Personal Connections Still Win in CRE

While CRE professionals acknowledge the importance of maintaining client relationships, research shows that many significantly underutilize their CRM systems. A 2020 Nucleus Research report found that less than half of CRM users leveraged advanced analytics or automation features fully. This gap suggests a major opportunity for improvement in adopting a more impactful, human-centered approach.

In essence, technology should facilitate—not replace—genuine, personal interactions. Personal relationships in commercial real estate remain paramount, and industry leaders consistently demonstrate that thoughtful human interactions create client loyalty and foster meaningful business relationships.

Real-World Examples of PIP in Action

Companies across various sectors provide powerful examples of what effective Personal Impact Programs look like in practice:

  • Chewy.com exemplifies this beautifully by sending handwritten notes and thoughtful gifts to customers experiencing the loss of a pet, demonstrating sincere compassion and empathy.
  • Ritz-Carlton hotels use CRM-driven insights to note guest preferences but empower their staff to proactively remember personal details—transforming routine stays into memorable, personalized experiences.
  • Zappos customer service teams regularly turn ordinary customer interactions into extraordinary moments by expressing empathy and sending personalized messages or gifts based on customer conversations.
  • LinkedIn’s Sales Navigator provides AI insights on leads, but the most successful salespeople personalize their outreach thoughtfully, congratulating contacts on career milestones rather than immediately pushing products.

These brands don’t just manage relationships—they proactively build them through genuine connections, guided and supported by CRM insights.

Launching Your Own Personal Impact Program

To build a successful PIP, follow these foundational practices:

  1. Deep Personalization: Move beyond automated insertions of names into emails. Understand your client's business, preferences, personal milestones, and use CRM insights to provide meaningful, relevant interactions.
  2. AI Insights with Human Execution: Allow your CRM and AI tools to offer data-driven insights and alerts. Train your team to respond in genuinely human, personalized ways.
  3. Surprise and Delight: Use CRM data to identify and reward your best clients or important contacts with unexpected gestures—personal notes, customized gifts, or thoughtful recognitions.
  4. Contextual and Timely Communication: Empower your team to choose the right moments to connect. Sometimes a casual, thoughtful check-in is worth more than a sales pitch, especially if timed strategically.

Technology Empowers but Doesn't Replace

Technology, CRM, and AI are powerful tools that amplify efficiency and productivity—but they will never replace human intuition, empathy, and authenticity. When blended thoughtfully through a clearly defined Personal Impact Program (PIP), these elements create client relationships marked by loyalty, trust, and mutual respect.

We'd love to hear about your experiences. What CRM platform is your team using? How do you integrate authentic personal interactions into your processes? Tell us about your Personal Impact Program—how does your team use technology to support, rather than replace, personal relationships in your business? Together, let's continue to prioritize meaningful connections that build lasting, successful partnerships in the evolving landscape of commercial real estate.

title: Your Logo Is NOT Your Brand (And Here’s Why That’s a Good Thing)
excerpt: Many mistake a logo for a brand, but your brand is much more. It’s the experience, perception, and emotional connection people have with your business. Logo…
body:
Many mistake a logo for a brand, but your brand is much more. It’s the experience, perception, and emotional connection people have with your business.

Logo vs. Brand

A logo is a visual identifier. Your brand is how people perceive you based on:

  • Your communication style
  • Customer experience
  • Company values
  • Your reputation

A great logo won’t build trust—your brand experience will.

Why This Matters in Real Estate

In real estate, branding is about relationships, trust, and reputation. Your logo won’t close deals—your client experience will.

  1. Trust & Credibility - Clients choose you for expertise, not a logo.
  2. Emotional Connection - People remember great service, not just visuals.
  3. Consistency - Your brand identity should be present in every interaction.
  4. Standing Out - Unique service makes you memorable, not just a design.

How to Build a Stronger Brand

  • Clear Messaging - Define and communicate your mission.
  • Consistent Identity - Beyond the logo, use cohesive visuals.
  • Exceptional Service - Ensure every touchpoint reflects your brand.
  • Thought Leadership - Share insights to build credibility.
  • Reputation Management - Engage with clients and gather reviews.

Final Thoughts

Your brand is not just a logo—it’s your impact, trust, and relationships. Invest in an authentic, strong brand, and the results will follow.

title: Why Investing in Your Brand Today Will Pay Off for Decades

body:
In the competitive world of real estate, branding isn’t just a logo or a tagline—it’s the foundation of long-term success. Developers, brokers, and marketing professionals who prioritize branding today set themselves up for sustainable growth, industry authority, and higher valuations down the road. Here’s why investing in your brand now will yield returns for decades.

1. Branding Builds Trust and Credibility

Real estate transactions involve significant financial commitments, and buyers, investors, and tenants want to work with brands they trust. A strong brand conveys reliability, consistency, and professionalism. When your brand is well-established, potential clients feel more confident in choosing your properties or services over competitors.

2. A Strong Brand Commands Premium Pricing

Would you rather be a commodity or a sought-after name? A well-developed brand allows real estate businesses to charge premium prices. When people recognize your name as synonymous with quality, they are willing to pay more—whether it’s for a property, brokerage service, or consulting.

3. Differentiation in a Crowded Market

With thousands of real estate firms and properties vying for attention, standing out is crucial. A strong brand highlights what makes you unique—whether it's your architectural style, customer service, or investment strategy. This differentiation creates a competitive edge that helps you attract and retain clients.

4. Stronger Marketing ROI

A clear and consistent brand identity amplifies marketing efforts. Instead of spending heavily on repetitive advertising just to remind people who you are, a recognizable brand makes every marketing dollar more effective. Your audience instantly connects your campaigns to the reputation you’ve built over time.

5. Brand Equity Increases Company Valuation

A well-established brand isn’t just a marketing tool—it’s a valuable business asset. Investors and buyers consider strong branding when assessing a company's worth. Real estate firms with recognized, reputable brands can command higher valuations, whether for raising capital or selling a business.

6. Attracting and Retaining Top Talent

A strong brand doesn’t just appeal to clients—it also attracts top-tier talent. Skilled brokers, architects, and marketing professionals want to align with brands that have a positive reputation and clear vision. Investing in your brand helps you build a team that drives success.

7. Future-Proofing Against Market Fluctuations

Market cycles shift, but strong brands endure. Companies that invest in branding are better positioned to weather economic downturns because their reputation continues to generate trust, referrals, and business even in uncertain times.

The Time to Invest Is Now

Branding isn’t an expense—it’s an investment with compounding returns. In real estate, where relationships and reputation drive success, the time to build a powerful brand is today. By focusing on trust, differentiation, and long-term recognition, you ensure your business remains relevant and profitable for years to come.

title: Then vs. Now: The Evolution of Real Estate Branding
excerpt: The landscape of real estate branding has undergone significant transformations over the past few decades. From traditional methods that emphasized physical…
body:
The landscape of real estate branding has undergone significant transformations over the past few decades. From traditional methods that emphasized physical presence and print media to contemporary strategies leveraging digital platforms and personalized experiences, the evolution reflects broader shifts in technology, consumer behavior, and market dynamics.

Traditional Real Estate Branding: The Foundation

In the past, real estate branding was heavily reliant on tangible assets and face-to-face interactions. Key components included:

  • Print Media and Signage: Agencies invested in newspaper advertisements, brochures, and prominent signage to capture local attention.
  • Personal Reputation: Success was often built on individual agents' reputations within their communities, emphasizing trust and personal relationships.
  • Physical Offices: A well-located office served as a testament to an agency's legitimacy and accessibility.

The Digital Revolution: A Paradigm Shift

The advent of the internet and digital technologies brought about a seismic shift in branding strategies:

  • Online Listings and Virtual Tours: Properties began to be showcased on websites with high-quality images and virtual tours, broadening the audience reach.
  • Social Media Engagement: Platforms like Instagram and Facebook became essential for marketing, allowing for targeted advertising and real-time interaction with potential clients.
  • Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Agencies optimized their online content to appear prominently in search results, increasing visibility.

Current Trends: Personalization and Authenticity

Today's branding strategies focus on creating personalized and authentic experiences:

  • Storytelling: Brands craft compelling narratives around properties and communities to engage clients emotionally.
  • User-Generated Content: Encouraging satisfied clients to share their experiences on social media adds credibility and fosters community.
  • Sustainability and Ethics: Highlighting eco-friendly practices and ethical considerations resonates with the modern, conscientious consumer.

The Role of Technology: AI and Beyond

Looking ahead, technology continues to drive innovation in real estate branding:

  • Artificial Intelligence (AI): AI is set to revolutionize design and marketing processes, enabling real-time creation of brand assets and content. This advancement allows for more agile and personalized marketing campaigns.
    Luxury Presence
  • Virtual and Augmented Reality: These technologies offer immersive property experiences, allowing potential buyers to explore spaces remotely.
  • Data Analytics: Leveraging data to understand consumer preferences enables more targeted and effective marketing strategies.

Conclusion

The evolution of real estate branding mirrors the industry's adaptation to technological advancements and changing consumer expectations. From traditional, relationship-based approaches to dynamic, technology-driven strategies, successful branding in real estate now demands a blend of authenticity, personalization, and innovation. As the industry continues to evolve, staying attuned to these trends will be crucial for real estate brokers, marketing specialists, and developers aiming to remain competitive and relevant.

title: From Cold to Gold: How AI-Enhanced Cold Calling is Driving Sales Success
excerpt: Cold calling has always had a bit of a bad reputation. Let’s face it—reaching out to strangers and trying to spark interest in your offering can feel like…
body:
Cold calling has always had a bit of a bad reputation. Let’s face it—reaching out to strangers and trying to spark interest in your offering can feel like climbing a steep hill with no end in sight. But here’s the good news: artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a powerful tool to make cold calling smarter, more efficient, and ultimately more rewarding.

If you’re in real estate—whether you’re an agent, developer, or part of a sales team—you’ll want to keep reading. AI is not here to replace your expertise or intuition, but it can support and enhance your approach, turning those “cold” calls into golden opportunities.

Why Cold Calling Has Always Been Tough

We’ve all been there: dialing number after number, hoping to find someone who will actually pick up and, even better, listen. Low response rates, a flood of rejections, and the sheer time it takes to sift through leads can drain your motivation fast.

But imagine a tool that helps you prioritize your efforts and makes it easier to connect with the right people. That’s where AI fits into the picture—not as a replacement but as an assistant to sharpen your process.

How AI Supports Smarter Cold Calling

AI isn’t a magic solution, but it can make your work more focused and effective. By leveraging AI as a tool in your toolkit, you can overcome some of the most frustrating parts of cold calling. Here’s how:

1. Focusing on High-Potential Leads

AI tools can analyze data to identify leads that are more likely to engage. While it won’t guarantee success, it can help you prioritize your time and energy, so you’re starting with the most promising prospects.

2. Adding a Personal Touch

No one wants to feel like they’re just another name on a call list. AI can help you prepare for conversations by offering insights into a prospect’s history, preferences, or online behavior. Armed with that information, you can create more meaningful and relevant conversations.

3. Providing Real-Time Support

During a call, AI tools can assist by suggesting ways to respond to objections or refining your messaging on the spot. But it’s still your voice, your rapport-building skills, and your ability to connect that will close the deal.

4. Saving Time on Prep Work

AI can streamline tedious tasks like sorting through leads or compiling prospect data, giving you more time to focus on what you do best: connecting with people and building relationships.

5. Learning from Experience

AI can analyze patterns and results after your calls, offering insights on what’s working and what could be improved. It’s like having a helpful assistant who keeps track of the small details, so you can focus on refining your strategy.

Real Success Stories in Real Estate

If you’re wondering whether this actually works, let me share a quick example. One real estate developer saw a 35% jump in lead conversions after adopting an AI-powered CRM. Their agents used the data-driven insights to target their efforts more effectively, while still relying on their own expertise to close deals. The combination of AI and human effort proved to be a winning formula.

What’s Next for AI in Sales?

The great thing about AI is that it’s not here to take over; it’s here to assist. As the tools become more advanced, they’ll offer even greater support for sales teams. For those in real estate, staying ahead of these trends is key to standing out in a competitive market.

Ready to Enhance Your Cold Calling Strategy?

If cold calls have been feeling more like a grind than an opportunity, consider how AI could become a valuable part of your process. Start small with tools like an AI-powered CRM or lead analysis software, and use them to complement—not replace—your unique skills.

Let’s keep the conversation going. What’s your take on AI in sales? Share your thoughts or drop a message if you’re curious about how AI can work for your business.

The way we think about office spaces is changing—and so are the expectations of tenants and employees. For real estate developers, agents, and corporate leaders, this is a chance to lead the way in creating workplaces built for today’s world.

A Moment of Change

What Employees Need

The one-size-fits-all office is a thing of the past. Today’s workforce craves flexibility, health and improved amenities: spaces for collaboration, quiet work, and designs that prioritize wellness with natural light, greenery, good air quality, places to entertain, exercise, shop, live and have fun. These aren’t just nice-to-haves—they’re must-haves.

Smarter Workspaces

Tenants want more than just a space—they want smart, connected environments with touchless tech, smart systems, and insights to make spaces work better. Artificial intelligence is going to play a major role in the office market during this year.

Shaping the Future

body:
Explore new concepts taking over social spaces

Eatertainment or Retailtainment
Brett Hunsaker and I recently connected with commercial real estate experts across the country to capture insights on the latest trends transforming the industry. We previously explored the impact of innovative amenities on themultifamily market, this time our focus is on the rise of “eatertainment” and “retailtainment.”

These trends — where retail, dining, and entertainment intersect — are reshaping traditional retail spaces and drawing in more consumers. As the commercial real estate landscape evolves, even office spaces, including repurposed buildings (see our “Obsolete office buildings” article on LinkedIn) and expansive, vacant spaces are embracing new concepts to boost leasing efforts with more unique amenities. Across the nation, we’re seeing a surge of creative venues like pickleball courts, mini-golf, and other social sports paired with vibrant dining and entertainment options.

Our survey gathered real-time examples of companies leading this charge, breathing new life into commercial spaces and energizing the real estate sector. Here’s an overview of the top concepts and the forward-thinking companies spearheading this exciting movement:

Pickleball & Dining Concepts
Pickleball, a paddle sport that combines elements of tennis, badminton, and ping-pong, is growing rapidly in popularity. Several new business models pair Pickleball with casual dining, craft beer, or other entertainment options.

Notable Companies and Examples

  • Chicken N Pickle: A fast-growing chain that blends Pickleball courts with a restaurant offering chicken-based dishes. It has locations across the U.S. and is expanding. https://chickennpickle.com

Axe throwing, which has become a popular social activity, combined with food and drinks, offering a unique entertainment experience.

Cigar and Whiskey Clubs

Notable Clubs

  • Wally’s Wine & Spirits (Los Angeles): Wally’s offers both a retail space and private club environment. The club hosts wine tastings, exclusive dining events, and has a membership option that gives access to high-end, rare wines and spirits, personalized storage lockers, and exclusive retail experiences. https://www.wallywine.com/

AMENITIES
Absolutely, there are many unique and unusual amenities that property owners, developers, and retailers are incorporating into their spaces to attract niche clientele, especially those with niche hobbies and specific passions. These amenities cater to affluent, VIP, or enthusiast groups and often blend lifestyle elements like community, privacy, and luxury into the experience. Unique Amenities

  • Car Vaults & Private Lounges: High-end auto storage clubs feature not only secure parking but also private lounges where members can meet and socialize.   • Events & Rallies: Many of these clubs host car shows, meetups, and driving rallies for their members.

NOTABLE EXAMPLES

2. Dog Parks & Pet-Friendly Amenities

  • Private Motor Condos (Chicago, IL): Offers storage units specifically for luxury car owners that include lounges, personal workshops, and private entertaining spaces. https://www.irongatemotorcondos.com/garages/

Conclusion
The retailtainment trend is rapidly expanding, with companies continually evolving to offer more immersive and interactive experiences. These new concepts appeal to a broad audience—from families seeking fun to corporate events and millennials looking for unique social outings.

Private social clubs are evolving beyond traditional members-only spaces, creating exclusive experiences that blend retail, dining, and entertainment. These venues are redefining luxury in a private setting.

By focusing on high-value services and unique community experiences, these concepts cater to affluent clients seeking beyond traditional retail or residential spaces. Incorporating amenities like luxury auto storage clubs, private dog parks, and high-end hobby-oriented communities provides property owners and developers with innovative ways to attract VIP clientele.

These evolving spaces redefine consumer expectations and foster community engagement. As demand for memorable experiences grows, developers and businesses have opportunities to create spaces that resonate with today’s experience-driven audiences. title: 2025 AI Trends in a Rapidly Evolving Real Estate Industry

body:
The real estate industry, as other industries are, is undergoing a revolutionary shift. Artificial Intelligence (AI), with its impressive potential, is changing how we buy, sell, and experience properties. This transformation isn't just about adopting new tools; it’s about envisioning a future where technology enhances human expertise.

AI: A New Ally in Real Estate

AI has evolved from a startling headlines into a vital asset for real estate professionals. Its capabilities extend across numerous areas, from predictive analytics to property branding. Here are a few impactful applications:

  1. Market Analysis and Forecasting: AI enables real-time analysis of market trends, helping investors and developers make informed decisions. By leveraging algorithms, it identifies growth areas, predicts price fluctuations, and optimizes investment strategies.
  1. Enhanced Property Branding: Storytelling, a cornerstone of branding, is now elevated with AI tools like MidJourney and Runway. These platforms create compelling visual narratives, capturing the essence of properties through generative imagery and video. For instance, crafting a brand identity for a historic building might involve AI-designed visuals showcasing its legacy and future potential​.
  1. Personalized Customer Experiences: From chatbots providing round-the-clock support to AI-driven virtual tours, the technology ensures prospective buyers and tenants have seamless interactions tailored to their needs.

How AI Trends Will Shape Real Estate in 2025

As we step into 2025, the intersection of AI and real estate is unveiling cutting-edge trends that promise to redefine the industry:

1. Generative Design in Architecture and Urban Planning

Generative AI tools are now widely adopted for designing architectural blueprints and urban layouts. They simulate real-time environmental factors, like energy efficiency and community traffic flow, creating smart cities that are both sustainable and efficient.

2. AI-Powered Smart Contracts

Blockchain combined with AI is streamlining transactions via smart contracts. These automated, secure agreements reduce administrative bottlenecks in real estate transactions, allowing faster, more transparent property exchanges.

3. Hyper-Personalized Marketing

In 2025, AI leverages behavioral data to craft hyper-personalized marketing strategies. For example, virtual reality (VR) property tours are dynamically adjusted based on user preferences, making them feel custom-designed for each client.

4. AI-Enhanced Retrofitting

Real estate developers are using AI to evaluate older properties for retrofitting opportunities. Algorithms identify structural weak points and suggest energy-efficient upgrades, extending the life of properties while aligning with green building initiatives.

5. Predictive Tenant Management

AI systems predict tenant needs before they arise, helping property managers maintain satisfaction and reduce turnover. For instance, predictive models can alert managers to likely maintenance issues, ensuring proactive resolutions.

6. Immersive AI in Real Estate Experiences

2025 sees the integration of immersive technologies like augmented reality (AR) and mixed reality (MR), powered by AI. These experiences allow potential buyers to "step into" a property or neighborhood virtually, experiencing it as if they were physically there.

The Inspirational Possibilities of AI-Driven Real Estate

AI is not just a tool but a catalyst for envisioning new possibilities. Imagine a future where:

  • Generative AI transforms underutilized office spaces into vibrant community hubs, addressing housing shortages and fostering urban innovation​.
  • Branding becomes more engaging, with AI crafting immersive campaigns that bridge the past, present, and future of properties.
  • Smart cities, designed with generative AI, provide sustainable living spaces for growing urban populations.

Overcoming Challenges with AI

While the opportunities are exciting, integrating AI into real estate is not without challenges:

  • Learning Curve: Understanding and deploying AI requires training and an open mindset.
  • Data Privacy: Handling client data responsibly is paramount.
  • Adaptation: As technology advances, staying updated is essential to maintain competitive advantage.

Building the Future

AI's impact on real estate is profound and far-reaching. For industry professionals, the journey begins with education. Engage with tools like ChatGPT, Claude, MidJourney and others for visual branding or to explore predictive analytics to anticipate market trends. Dive into the wealth of AI resources available to uncover innovative ways to enhance your strategies.

As we stand on the edge of this transformation, one thing is clear: AI is not here to replace the human touch but to amplify it. By embracing this technology, real estate professionals can unlock new heights of creativity, efficiency, and impact.

title: The Advantages and Risks of Subleasing Commercial Space During the Holidays

body:
The holiday season often brings unique opportunities for businesses and landlords in the commercial real estate market. Subleasing commercial space during this period can be a smart move, but it comes with both risks and rewards. Here’s a closer look at the potential benefits and challenges.

Advantages of Subleasing During the Holidays

🎁 Boosting Cash Flow

For companies with unused office or retail space, subleasing can generate extra income during a time when costs like bonuses and year-end expenses may strain budgets.

📈 Meeting Seasonal Demand

Short-term tenants — such as pop-up shops or seasonal businesses — often seek temporary spaces during the holidays, creating a surge in demand for subleases.

🌟 Building Relationships

Subleasing can foster relationships with businesses that might become long-term tenants or partners.

Risks of Holiday Subleasing

❄️ Temporary Tenants

Short-term leases carry the risk of tenant turnover and the associated administrative burden of re-leasing the space.

🔧 Wear and Tear

Increased foot traffic during the busy holiday season can lead to greater wear and tear, increasing maintenance costs.

📋 Lease Compliance Issues

Some primary lease agreements restrict subleasing, creating legal or financial risks if the process isn’t carefully managed.

Best Practices for Subleasing

  • Screen Tenants Carefully: Vet potential subtenants for financial stability and reputation to avoid future headaches.
  • Check Lease Terms: Ensure subleasing complies with your primary lease to avoid penalties.
  • Draft a Clear Sublease Agreement: Outline responsibilities, costs, and expectations to protect both parties.
  • Prepare for a Quick Turnaround: Be ready to market and finalize agreements quickly to take advantage of holiday demand.

The Bottom Line

Subleasing during the holidays can provide significant financial and strategic advantages, but only when approached carefully. By understanding the risks and following best practices, landlords and tenants can make the most of this seasonal opportunity.

title: How the New Trump Administration Could Impact the Housing Real Estate Market

body:
As a new administration takes office, policy shifts could significantly influence the U.S. housing market. 

The Trump administration has outlined several proposals, ranging from regulatory reform to changes in immigration and mortgage policies, all of which could have far-reaching effects on housing affordability, supply and market stability.

Regulatory Reforms and Housing Supply

The Trump administration aims to reduce regulations affecting housing construction. President-elect Trump has noted that regulatory costs account for about 30% of the price of a new home. His administration plans to cut these costs and open portions of federal land for large-scale housing construction. 

If implemented effectively, these reforms could lower building expenses, increase the housing supply, and address affordability issues.

Immigration Policies and Construction Labor

Proposals to tighten immigration laws and deport undocumented immigrants could lead to labor shortages in the construction industry. Immigrants make up about 30% of the U.S. construction workforce, and a decrease in available labor could drive up costs for builders and slow down new housing developments. This could counteract efforts to increase the housing supply and exacerbate affordability challenges.

Mortgage Rates and Financial Markets

The administration’s economic agenda, including proposed tax cuts and increased infrastructure spending, could lead to higher inflation and government debt. These factors may result in higher mortgage rates, which have already been on the rise. 

Higher rates could make it harder for first-time buyers to enter the market and deter current homeowners from selling, slowing the overall housing market.

Affordable Housing Initiatives

To address housing affordability, the administration plans to make federal land available for development and reduce construction costs through deregulation. While these efforts could alleviate the housing shortage, their success depends on implementation and whether designated federal lands are in areas of high demand.

Potential Privatization of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac

Republicans have long advocated for the privatization of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, two critical entities in the U.S. mortgage market. Privatization aims to reduce government oversight and taxpayer risk but could lead to higher borrowing costs for homebuyers. 

This shift may have a particularly significant impact on low- and middle-income families seeking affordable financing options.

What to Expect Moving Forward

The Trump administration’s policies could bring both opportunities and challenges to the housing market. While regulatory reforms and increased land availability might boost supply, labor shortages and rising mortgage rates could hinder affordability and development. 

Also, the privatization of key mortgage institutions could reshape the housing finance landscape.

Stakeholders in the real estate industry should closely monitor these policy changes to anticipate market trends and adapt accordingly.

What do you think?

How do you see these potential policies shaping your local housing market?

title: AI is taking over CRE Training! Not so fast…

body:
A Closer Look at the Balance Between Technology and Personal Interaction

The world of real estate is ever evolving, especially with recent technological advancements. Today Artificial Intelligence (AI) is impacting every facet of our professional and personal lives. We’re seeing it used for a variety of administrative tasks, data analysis, creative concepts, and so much more. In this article we explore the debate around AI-assisted coaching in the professional setting to provide insights into future coaching for real estate professionals. Let’s start by taking a look at the advantages and disadvantages of both AI-driven coaching and person-to-person coaching.

THE RISE OF AI-DRIVEN COACHING

AI-driven coaching leverages the vast information used to train them. Using these platforms have several key advantages across a number sectors. 

Accessibility and Cost-Effectiveness

AI coaching tools are available around the clock, providing support when needed. This 24/7 availability is useful for professionals, especially those in real estate, who often work irregular hours. Questions and concerns often come at the times when we’re not with our coaches. These tools offer an opportunity to get feedback and understanding right when we may need it. 

There are several business coaches and entrepreneurs who are either already using or working on AI-coaching bots to reach greater numbers of individuals (Chris Do’s DoBot and Daymond John’s Daymond On Demand). They have integrated their works, thoughts and ideas into an AI platform. When the bot is asked a question it responds, based on the given information, as the coach naturally would to that type of inquiry.

AI also has greater scalability and can reach many people simultaneously. This makes coaching accessible to those who may not have the means to afford in-person coaching.

Consistency, Objectivity and Personalization

AI can analyze vast amounts of data to help track progress and improvement. It can produce more consistent feedback where human coaches may vary. Using AI to assist in coaching can reduce human biases. It can be found to offer more fair and unbiased feedback based directly on collected data.

Deep analysis of this type allows for highly personalized training programs based on individual data. It also allows for adapting in real-time to the user’s progress and needs.

IN-PERSON COACHING: THE HUMAN CONNECTION

In-person coaching brings its own unique advantages which AI cannot replicate. As we investigate how A.I. will be a significant player in both coaching and training, I always refer to my expert in commercial real estate (CRE), Brett Hunsaker, to get his input on the AI phenomenon versus in-person coaching and training. With 35+ years of managing producers, Brett has worked with many of the top training groups in the industry and gave me the following pointers on why it’s still very important to have in-person coaching and training as part of your salesforce development plan:

Emotional Intelligence: In-person coaching provides emotional and psychological support. Human trainers and coaches can understand and respond to the emotional states and needs of their trainees. They can provide empathy, encouragement, and motivation, which are critical for effective learning and personal development. 

Personalized Feedback: In-person coaching allows for real-time, nuanced feedback tailored to the individual's specific needs and learning style. Coaches can observe body language, tone of voice, and other non-verbal cues to give more comprehensive feedback.

Relationship Building: In-person interactions foster relationships and trust, which are crucial for a productive coaching environment. A strong coach-trainee relationship can lead to greater openness, confidence, and a willingness to take risks and make mistakes, which are essential for growth.

Motivation and Accountability: The presence of a human coach can provide a stronger sense of accountability and motivation. Knowing that someone is invested in their progress can push trainees to stay committed and put in the effort needed to achieve their goals.

Support and Encouragement: In-person coaches can offer genuine support and encouragement, celebrating successes and helping to navigate setbacks. This emotional support is vital for maintaining morale and resilience during challenging times.

Networking Opportunities: In-person training often provides opportunities for trainees to network with their peers and other professionals. These connections can lead to valuable relationships, collaborations, and career opportunities.

Adaptability: Human coaches can adapt their training methods on the fly based on the trainee's progress and responses. They can adjust the pace, change strategies, and address individual challenges more effectively than AI, which may follow a more rigid structure. Human coaches are better able to adapt to unforeseen situations and provide immediate, intuitive responses during sessions. Experienced coaches bring a wealth of knowledge and practical expertise offering more nuanced guidance than current AI tools. In-person coaches have the ability to offer more holistic approaches. Approaches addressing not only professional training but mental, emotional and lifestyle components.

Cultural and Contextual Understanding: Human coaches bring cultural awareness and context-specific knowledge that AI may lack. They can understand and incorporate the unique cultural, social, and organizational dynamics that influence learning and performance.

Complex Problem Solving: Some issues and challenges are complex and require a deep understanding of human behavior and organizational dynamics. Human coaches are better equipped to navigate and address these complexities, drawing on their experience and intuition.

Flexibility in Communication: Human coaches can communicate in diverse and flexible ways, using humor, storytelling, and other techniques to engage and inspire trainees. This level of dynamic communication is often beyond the capabilities of AI.

POTENTIAL CONCERNS

Both in-person and AI-driven coaching come with their own drawbacks and tradeoffs. While AI-assisted training and coaching can offer convenience, consistency, and scalability, the personal touch of in-person coaching brings a depth of understanding, connection, and adaptability that is difficult to replicate with technology alone. AI lacks emotional intelligence and empathy of human coaches. A component crucial in the coaching relationship. AI relies only on the data it is given which may not always capture the full picture of the challenges and needs of the individual. We should also consider algorithmic bias. AI can preserve bias present in the data with which it was trained or the biases of the programmers themselves.

Security and privacy are important to coaches and the individuals they serve. Compliance with privacy regulations and safeguarding user information is vital. 

As human we all have the same 24 hours to fit in our day. This limits the time and availability of any coach, making it harder to access them as frequently as may be needed. In-person coaching can be expensive, thus limiting access for many people.

A BLENDED APPROACH

When human and AI combine their talents, skills and abilities we find amazing results. The blended approach maximizes engagements and learning opportunities and outcomes.

Coaches can utilize AI to assist with data analysis, creation of personalized training plans and facilitate real-time feedback. AI is able to handle routine administrative tasks, such as scheduling, progress tracking and assessments. This frees up human coaches to focus on other aspects of coaching, allowing them to maintain emotional support, complex problem-solving and offering holistic guidance. 

Brett and I surveyed top training/coaching experts in CRE to get their perspective on AI training and coaching. 

The Massimo Group (https://massimo-group.com/), led by Rod Santomassimo, is using AI to augment their services and processes. This year they launched role-play and closing chatbots as well as their Resource Library Bot and Virtual Coach. These tools have been trained with the expertise and content developed during years of coaching. With AI-assistance they also redeployed their video content in multiple languages allowing further reach and accessibility. Regarding AI, Rod said, “I do not see where AI will replace human coaches in the short term (5 years). Indeed, not at the Massimo Group. AI will be leveraged to assist our clients when our human resources are unavailable and supplement our human coaches in our content delivery.”

ETC (https://ericthecoach.com/) founder Eric Moore takes an AI-assisted approach to his work with clients. He flips the script on coaching by turning the AI spotlight on himself. Instead of guiding his clients, he throws his own coaching transcripts into the AI mix, prompting it to suggest ways he can up his game. Eric also uses AI tools to help shorten the coaching lifecycle. Tools which enable individuals to upload questions, concerns and follow up between sessions. It then creates a report which can be used before and during the next face-to-face session. He uses a variety of complex prompts for session summaries and for self-evaluation to help him grow as a coach. Eric notes, “using the Socratic method as a prompt approach has been a game-changer to my use of Large Language Models (LLMs).”

Mike Lipsey president of The Lipsey Company (https://lipseyco.com/) states he’s “a huge fan of the contribution that AI will make in commercial real estate.” He and his team are utilizing AI to assist in many areas. These range from lease abstracts, proposal comparisons and calculations, proposal creation, letters of intent (LOI), and much more. When asked about AI taking over coaching and training Mike said, “in the short term, absolutely not.” He further notes a question he is frequently asked is “what’s the most important skill I need to be successful in commercial real estate?” His answer – social skills. “Knowing how to create rapport, be charming, and empathic all at the same time is a unique capability. Trainers and coaches need to have similar social skills that a successful broker possess. As of today, I’ve not seen any demonstration on AI’s part that has the energy and sense of humor of a competent trainer and coach.”

Ed Riggins head of Riggo & Co. (https://edriggins.com/) echoed the thoughts of Mike and Rod but emphasized that, “empathy is a key element of emotional intelligence. It's because of my capacity for empathy that my coaching clients tell me things they would never tell a chat bot.” While AI will play a part in coaching and training, he advocates for the human touch. He doesn’t see a time in the near future where an AI will make a person “feel know and cared for.” Ed sees a future in which, “what will be in high demand will be human beings who have a sense of humor, crazy-good listening skills, and the demonstrated ability to genuinely give a damn about other human beings.”

USE CASES FOR AI COACHING IN REAL ESTATE

AI can analyze vast amounts of data, enabling it to identity strengths, weaknesses and learning preferences of individuals. Information which can be used to create customized development plans tailored to a person’s unique needs. Utilizing the personalized plan in conjunction with real-time feedback can fine-tune coaching strategies. A continuous feedback loop between the user and the AI tool helps in faster skill acquisition and development. Experienced real estate coaches and mentors can access reports to see how younger professionals are progressing and make needed adjustments and provide in-person support. Using a combination of AI and human coaches can support thousands of real estate professionals simultaneously. This provides consistent, high-quality coaching across an organization.

The Future of AI in Real Estate Coaching

AI coaching will improve over the next few years. Advancements in recognition of tone and body language, and real-time analysis will enhance its effectiveness. As our experts noted, AI is unlikely to replace the need for the human factor. The hybrid model with AI supporting human coaches is the projected outcome. Combining the strengths of both approaches will create a more available, scalable and comprehensive experience for all.

Conclusion

Integrating AI into real estate coaching offers significant benefits, including increased accessibility, cost-effectiveness, and personalized training. However, the irreplaceable value of direct, human-to-human engagement underscores the importance of maintaining in-person coaching as the cornerstone of professional development. By adopting a blended approach, combining the strengths of both AI and human coaches, real estate professionals can achieve optimal learning outcomes and drive success in their careers.

References

Biswa, S. (2024). Transforming Development: AI-Powered Coaching and Mentoring. LinkedIn.

Chatterjee, K. (2024). Can Virtual Coaching Platforms and AI-driven Coaching Tools Hit the Mark? LinkedIn.

Fletcher, M. (2024). Seven Benefits of AI Coaching in Achieving Professional Growth. Mindbeat.

Pappas, C. (2024). The Future of AI Coaching: How Can You Leverage It? eLearning Industry.

Syam, B. (2024). Transforming Development: AI-Powered Coaching and Mentoring. LinkedIn.
